8.1: So Dar: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. What is that gate of yours like, and what is that home like, where (you) sit and take care of all? The sounds of your countless instruments of many kinds play there, and so many are the musicians who play for you. So many of your ragas, with their raginis, are sung there, and so many are your singers. Wind, water and fire sing of you; Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) sings of you at your door. Chitr and Gupt, who know how to write, sing of you; what they write, Dharam Raj weighs and judges. Shiva, Brahma and the goddesses sing of you, ever beautiful, adorned by you. The Indras, seated on their thrones, sing of you with the gods at your door. The Siddhas sing of you in samadhi (deep meditative absorption); the sadhus sing of you in contemplation. The celibates, the charitable and the contented sing of you; the mighty heroes sing of you. The pandits and the great rishis who read (the scriptures) sing of you, age after age, along with the Vedas. The enchanting women who charm the mind sing of you, in heaven, in the mortal world and in the netherworld. The jewels you have created sing of you, along with the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. Warriors of great might and heroes sing of you; the four sources of life sing of you. The regions, the worlds and the universes, made and set in place by you, sing of you. They alone sing of you who please you, your devotees, steeped (in your love) and full of delight. So many others sing of you who do not come to my mind; what can Nanak consider? He, he alone, is ever true; the Master is true, and true is his glory. He is, and he will be; he does not depart, nor will he depart, he who made the creation. He who brought forth Maya of many colours, many kinds and many species watches over what he has made, having made it, as befits his greatness. Whatever pleases him, that he will do; no command can then be given (to him). He is the King, the Emperor over kings; O Nanak, (our part is) to live in his will. ॥1॥
Dharam Raj judges each soul by its deeds; Chitr and Gupt are, by tradition, the two recorders at his court who write down the deeds of every being.

Mach is the mortal world, between heaven and the netherworld. The jewels: by tradition, the fourteen jewels that came out of the ocean when it was churned. The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are the tiraths held most holy in India.
The four sources of life (khaani): birth from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth.
9.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Everyone calls you great, (O God,) having heard (it from others), but how great you are is (told) only on seeing you. Your worth cannot be fixed, nor can you be put into words. Those who speak of you stay merged in you. O my great Master, deep and profound, fathomless in virtues, no one knows how much, how vast, your expanse is. All who practise surat (attention fixed on God) joined together and practised it; all who weigh worth joined together and weighed (yours); yet by the men of knowledge, the men of meditation, the teachers and the teachers of teachers, not even a sesame seed's worth of your greatness could be told. All truthfulness, all austerities, all good deeds, and the great powers of the Siddhas, the accomplished ones: without you, no one has attained this siddhi (accomplishment). It comes by (your) grace, and then no one can hold it back. What can the poor speaker (say)? Your storehouses are filled with praises. The one to whom you give (your praise), what can anyone do against him? O Nanak, the True One (himself) is the one who adorns (him). ॥4॥
The Siddhas are yogis held to have reached perfection; siddhi is attainment, the miraculous powers among it.
9.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When I utter (his Name), I live; when it is forgotten, I die. The True Name is hard to utter. If hunger for the True Name arises, then, eating (of the Name) in that hunger, the sorrows are driven away. Why should he be forgotten, O my mother? The Master is true, and (is found) through the True Name. Of the True Name's greatness, even a sesame seed's worth, they have grown weary telling, yet none has found its worth. If all were to join together and set about describing him, he does not become greater, nor does he become less. He does not die, nor is there mourning (for him). He keeps on giving, and what he gives to be enjoyed never runs out. This is his quality: there is no other (like him); none has been, and none will be. As great as you yourself are, so great is your gift, (you,) who made the day and made the night. Those who forget the Master are low-born; O Nanak, those without the Name are the outcastes. ॥4॥
Kamjaat (low-born) and sanaat (counted outside the four castes) are not caste by birth here: the Guru says the low are those who forget the Master.
10.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O servant of the Lord, True Guru, True Being, I make my plea before you, Guru: we are lowly worms and insects, True Guru, come to your refuge; be merciful, and make the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) shine (in us). O my friend, divine Guru, make the Lord's Name shine in me. May the Naam, received through the Guru's teaching, be the companion of my life, and the Lord's praise my provision for the road. Great, very great, is the fortune of the Lord's servants who have faith in the Lord, Har Har, and a thirst for the Lord. On receiving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; and in the Sangat (the company of the holy), virtues shine forth in them. Those who have not found the Lord's sweet essence, the Naam, are unfortunate, and in the grip of Jam (the messenger of Death). Those who have not come to the True Guru's refuge and his Sangat: cursed is their living, and cursed their hope of life. The servants of the Lord who have found the True Guru's Sangat had this written on their foreheads by the Lord from the start. Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), in which the Lord's sweet essence is found; O Nanak, in meeting the Lord's servants, the Naam shines forth within. ॥4॥
Rahraas: the provisions for a journey; for the journey of life, the Lord's praise. The evening bani, Rehras, takes its name from it.
10.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, why do you keep brooding over your efforts (to earn), when the dear Lord is engaged in the task (of caring for you)? He has created creatures in rocks and stones, and set their food ready for them beforehand. O my dear Lord (Madho), whoever has joined the Sat Sangat has crossed over. By the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state; the dry wood has turned green. Mother, father, people, sons, wife: no one is anyone's support. The Master delivers sustenance to each and every one; O mind, why are you afraid? (The crane) comes flying hundreds of kos (leagues), her little ones left behind. Who is there to feed them, to give them grain to peck? She keeps them remembered in her mind. All the treasures and the eighteen siddhis rest in the palm of the Master's hand. O servant Nanak, let us be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to him; (O Lord,) your extent has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥4॥
Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God.
The crane (koonj) flies hundreds of kos in winter, leaving her young behind.
The treasures: by tradition, the nine treasures (nidhis). The eighteen siddhis: the miraculous powers of yoga, eight of them (anima, laghima and the rest) the best known.
